summary: harness gc --deps deletes DEPS_DIRS (default node_modules .next .next-check .venv) in worktrees of ended runs, merged or not: meta.env WT= must name the worktree; no live driver, queued continuation or open desk; never the checkout, a symlink, a path out of the tree or tracked files. Prints '+ freed <n> MB in <wt>: <dirs>' / 'would: freed'. 3 checks; decision, README, architecture §3/§10.
verified_how: RED first: 312/314 (two new --deps checks failed on 'unknown option'); then lib/check.sh green, 314/314. KEEP=1 run: gcd1/gcd2 output read by hand (one freed line, deps-end only).

dead_ends.tried: the queued-continuation check as `! grep -q deps-q`
dead_ends.why: the branch pass prints '! failed: branch -d harness/deps-q' (merged branch checked out in a worktree); narrowed to the freed line

discoveries.text: cmd_gc's branch passes try `branch -d` on merged branches checked out in a worktree (a live or queued run's, a dirty one gc kept): git refuses, gc prints 'error: cannot delete branch … used by worktree' and '! failed: …'. Harmless but noisy; the passes could skip branches `running` or listed in `git worktree list`.

--deps runs after the worktree removal loop and reads DEPS_DIRS via harness_config "$p" in a subshell (user config, then the checkout's .harness/config.sh). tests/run.sh has gd_run <run> [<wt>] (state dir with ended + meta.env, worktree on harness/<run> at origin/main, node_modules/x.js).
